dm: One should respectfully accept upon one's head The words of those skilled in advising others And who provide unsolicited benefit; Always remain a student to everyone.
gm: Skilled in exhorting others, and Words that act beneficially unasked, Accept them with respect upon your crown, and Always become the disciple of everyone.

dm: To all that is well-spoken, One should say, "It is excellently said." When seeing someone performing a meritorious deed, Generate joy by praising them well.
gm: To all words that are well spoken, You should say, "Excellently spoken." If you see someone creating merit, Generate joy well by praising them.

dm: Speak of virtues in private, And when virtues are spoken of, join in. When one's own virtues are spoken of, Recognize it as an appreciation of qualities.
gm: Speak of good qualities in secret, And if good qualities are spoken of, join in. If your own good qualities are spoken of, Understand that as them knowing good qualities.

dm: All such endeavors are for the sake of joy, Which is rare even if one were to buy it with wealth. Therefore, through the virtues performed by others, One should enjoy the happiness of being joyful.
gm: All undertakings are for the sake of joy, Yet that is rare even if bought with a price. Therefore, through the good qualities achieved by others, I should enjoy the happiness of joy.

dm: In this, there is no loss for oneself, And in the next life, there will be great happiness; Through wrongdoing, one is unhappy and suffers, And in the next life, the suffering will be even greater.
gm: In this, there is no loss for me here, And in the next life there is great happiness. Through faults there is unhappiness and suffering, And in the next life there is great suffering.

dm: When speaking, one should speak in a way that is agreeable, coherent, And clear in meaning, and pleasant; Free from attachment and aversion, One should speak gently and in moderation.
gm: When speaking, comforting and coherent, Clear in meaning and pleasing to the mind, Having abandoned attachment and hatred, One should speak gently and in moderation.

dm: Even when looking at sentient beings with one's eyes, One should think, "It is by relying on these very beings That I shall attain Buddhahood," And look upon them with a straightforward and loving manner.
gm: Even when looking at sentient beings with your eyes, Thinking, "Relying precisely upon them, I will become a Buddha," You should look with a direct and loving manner.

dm: Whether motivated by constant devotion Or by the application of an antidote, Great virtue arises toward those who possess qualities, Those who have been helpful, and those who are suffering.
gm: Motivated by constant strong aspiration, Or motivated by the antidote, Towards the fields of qualities and benefactors, And the suffering, virtue becomes great.

dm: Having become skillful and endowed with initiative, I shall always perform my tasks. In all activities, one should not Depend upon anyone else.
gm: Being skilled and endowed with faith, I should always perform actions myself. In all actions, upon anyone at all, I should not rely.

dm: One should practice the perfections, such as generosity, In an ever-ascending degree of excellence. One should not sacrifice a great benefit for a small one; The primary consideration should be the welfare of others.
gm: The perfection of generosity and the rest, Should be practiced, progressing higher and higher. One should not abandon the greater for the lesser. Principally, one should consider the benefit of others.

dm: Having understood this, one should always Remain diligent in working for the welfare of others. Because the Compassionate One sees far ahead, He permits even those things that were prohibited.
gm: Having understood thus, for the benefit of others, One should always remain striving. By the Compassionate One who sees far, Even prohibited actions have been permitted for that.

dm: One should share with those who have fallen into wrong paths, the protectorless, And those established in ascetic vows; One should eat only in moderation, And give away everything except for the three religious robes.
gm: To those fallen into ruin, the unprotected, And those abiding in ascetic practice, one should share; One should eat only a moderate amount, And give away everything except the three Dharma robes.

dm: This body, which practices the sublime Dharma, Should not be harmed for the sake of something minor. By acting in this way, the aspirations Of sentient beings will be swiftly fulfilled.
gm: The body that practices the sublime Dharma Should not be harmed for trivial reasons. If one acts thus, the wishes of sentient beings Will quickly be fulfilled.

dm: As long as the compassionate intention is not pure, One should not give away this body; Rather, in this and other lives as well, It should be given as a cause for accomplishing the great purpose.
gm: As long as the thought of compassion is impure, This body should not be given away; Rather, in this and other lives as well, It should be given as a cause to accomplish a great purpose.

dm: Do not teach the Dharma to those who are disrespectful. Do not teach those who, unless they are ill, wear turbans, Carry parasols, staffs, or weapons, Or have their heads covered.
gm: One should not explain the Dharma to the disrespectful, Nor to those who wear head-wraps while not sick, Nor to those holding umbrellas, staffs, or weapons, Nor to those whose heads are covered.

dm: Do not teach the profound and vast to those of lesser inclination, Nor to a woman without a man present. Toward both the lesser and the supreme teachings, One should always act with equal respect.
gm: Nor the profound and vast to the inferior, Nor to a woman without a man present. To the inferior and supreme Dharmas, One should apply equal respect in all cases.

dm: One who has become a vessel for the vast Dharma Should not be applied to the lesser Dharma. One must not completely forsake proper conduct, Nor deceive others with Sutra or Mantra.
gm: One who is a vessel for the vast Dharma Should not be engaged in the inferior Dharma; Conduct should not be completely cast aside, Nor should they be deceived with sutras and mantras.

dm: When discarding tooth-sticks or spitting, One should cover them. It is also criticized to discharge urine and so forth Into water or onto land intended for use.
gm: Tooth-sticks and saliva, When discarded, should be covered; Also, urine and the like, into usable Water or on land, it is deprecated to discard.

dm: Do not eat with a full mouth, with noise, Or with the mouth wide open. Do not sit with legs stretched out, And do not rub your hands together.
gm: With a full mouth, making noise, And with an open mouth, one should not eat; One should not sit with legs outstretched, And one should not rub the hands together.

dm: In vehicles, on beds, or in dwellings, Do not remain alone with another's wife. Having observed and inquired, Avoid everything that causes the world to lose faith.
gm: In vehicles, beds, and seats, One should not be alone with another's woman. Everything that causes the world to lose faith, Having observed and inquired, one should abandon.

dm: One should not make gestures with the fingers; Rather, with a gesture of respect, One should use the entire right hand To indicate the way in that manner.
gm: One should not indicate with a finger, But respectfully, with the right Hand used entirely, Even the path should be shown in this way.

dm: Do not wave your arms excessively; Move them only slightly and make a sound, Such as snapping your fingers, to give a signal; Otherwise, you will be acting without restraint.
gm: One should not wave the arms wildly, But move them slightly, making a sound By snapping the fingers and so forth as a sign; Otherwise, one will be uncontrolled.

dm: Just as the Protector lay when passing into nirvana, One should lie down in the desired direction; From the very beginning, firmly apply the intention To wake up quickly with alertness.
gm: Just as the Lord lay when passing into nirvana, One should lie down in the desired direction; With clear comprehension and the thought of rising quickly, One should definitely set the mind from the very beginning.

dm: Although the conduct of Bodhisattvas Is said to be immeasurable, One should certainly practice those activities That serve to train the mind.
gm: The practices of the Bodhisattvas Are taught to be limitless; The practice of purifying the mind, One should definitely practice at least that much.

dm: Three times during the day and three times at night, One should recite the Three Heaps Sūtra; By relying on the Victors and the spirit of awakening, One should pacify the remaining downfalls.
gm: Three times during the day and night, One should recite the Triskandha; By relying on the Conquerors and the awakening mind, One should pacify the remainder of downfalls thereby.

dm: Whether by one's own power or the influence of others, In whatever situation or whatever one is doing, One should diligently train in whatever Has been taught as the training for that occasion.
gm: Whether under one's own or another's power, In whatever situation, whatever one is doing, Whatever has been taught as a training, In that situation, one should exert oneself and train.

dm: There is nothing whatsoever That the Sons of the Victors should not learn; For the wise who abide in this way, There is no merit that does not accrue.
gm: That which is not to be trained in by the Sons of the Conqueror, Does not exist at all; For the wise one who abides in this way, There is nothing that does not become merit.

dm: Whether directly or indirectly, Do nothing other than act for the benefit of sentient beings; Solely for the sake of sentient beings, Dedicate everything toward enlightenment.
gm: Whether directly or else indirectly, One should do nothing other than the benefit of sentient beings; For the sake of sentient beings alone, One should dedicate everything for awakening.

dm: One should never forsake a spiritual friend Who is learned in the meaning of the Mahāyāna And possesses the supreme conduct of a Bodhisattva, Even at the cost of one's own life.
gm: Always, the virtuous spiritual friend, Who is skilled in the meaning of the Mahāyāna, And the supreme discipline of the bodhisattvas, Should not be given up even for the sake of one's life.

dm: Learn the manner of relying on a guru As described in the life story of Śrīsambhava; This and other teachings of the Buddha Are to be understood by reading the sūtras.
gm: From the liberation story of Śrīsaṃbhava, One should train in the manner of relying on the guru; This and other words spoken by the Buddha, Should be known after reading the sūtras.

dm: The trainings are revealed within the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, in particular, Should be looked at first of all.
gm: The trainings appear in the sūtras, Therefore, one should read the sūtras; The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra, Should be looked at from the very beginning.

dm: Because it extensively demonstrates What must be practiced at all times, The Śikṣāsamuccaya as well Should certainly be looked at again and again.
gm: Because what is to be practiced constantly Is extensively taught in that, The Śikṣāsamuccaya, too, Should definitely be looked at again and again.

dm: Alternatively, for the time being, one should look at the concise Compendium of Sūtras; Both works composed by the noble Nāgārjuna should also be studied with diligence.
gm: Or else, for the time being, the brief Sūtrasamuccaya should be looked at; And the two composed by the Noble Nāgārjuna Should also be looked at with effort.

dm: Whatever is not prohibited therein Is exactly what should be practiced; In order to guard the minds of worldly beings, Having seen the trainings, one should practice them correctly.
gm: Whatever is not forbidden by whichever, That itself should be practiced; In order to guard the minds of worldly beings, Having seen the trainings, one should practice perfectly.

dm: Regarding the state of one's body and mind, One should examine them again and again; This alone, in brief, Is the definition of guarding introspection.
gm: The states of the body and mind, Should be examined again and again; That alone, in brief, Is the defining characteristic of guarding introspection.

dm: These must be practiced with the body; What can be accomplished by merely speaking words? Will a sick person be benefited By merely reading a medical treatise?
gm: These should be practiced with the body; What will be accomplished by merely uttering words? By merely reading a medical treatise, Will patients be benefited?

dm: This concludes the fifth chapter, "Guarding Introspection," from the *Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva*.
gm: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the fifth chapter: Guarding Introspection.
